> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text

```

```text
Add a button tile to a native dashboard via :addChart. Button tiles
```

## dashboards charts add

Add a chart with a YARA-L query to a dashboard (guarded)

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl dashboards charts add <dashboard-id> --title <t> (--query <yaral> | --query-file <f>) [flags]
```

```text
Add a chart to a native dashboard via :addChart, authoring its YARA-L query
inline (the dashboard body itself is reference-only, so `push dashboards`
cannot do this). The query comes from --query or --query-file.

Chart type: pass --chart-type area|bar|gauge|line|map|metrics|pie|scatter|table
with --x/--y (encode
variables) and optional --series-by to GENERATE the visualization instead of
hand-authoring --visualization; --x/--y/--series-by are validated against the
query's declared match:/outcome: variables, so a typo fails clean (not a blank
chart). --if-absent skips the add when a chart with the same title already
exists (idempotent re-runs). Guarded: dry-run by default, --yes to apply.
Re-pull afterwards so local mirrors live.

RESERVED WORDS: avoid these as $variable names — they compile but 400 at
execute time (blank chart): rule, private, global, meta, strings, condition,
events, match, outcome, options, dedup, order, limit, select, unselect, and,
or, not, all, any, at, contains, startswith, endswith, icontains, istartswith,
iendswith, iequals, matches, in, over, nocase, ascii, wide, fullword, xor,
base64, base64wide, filesize, entrypoint, int8..uint32/be variants.
Rename collisions (e.g. $rule → $rule_v) before adding.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--chart-type` | string | - | generate the visualization: area \| bar \| gauge \| line \| map \| metrics \| pie \| scatter \| table |
| `--datasource` | string | {"dataSources":["UDM"]} | chart datasource (JSON) |
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--if-absent` | bool | false | skip the add when a chart with the same title already exists (idempotent) |
| `--interval` | string | {"relativeTime":{"timeUnit":"DAY","startTimeVal":"1"}} | query input interval (JSON) |
| `--layout` | string | {"startX":0,"spanX":96,"startY":0,"spanY":16} | chart layout on the 96-column grid (JSON: startX/spanX 0–96, startY/spanY); default is full-width |
| `--no-filters` | bool | false | do not bind the chart to the dashboard's GlobalTimeFilter |
| `--query` | string | - | inline YARA-L query for the chart |
| `--query-file` | string | - | read the YARA-L query from a file |
| `--series-by` | string | - | --chart-type bar\|line: split into stacked series by this query variable |
| `--tile-type` | string | visualization | tile type: visualization \| button |
| `--title` | string | - | chart display name (required) |
| `--visualization` | string | - | optional raw visualization config (JSON); or use --chart-type to generate it |
| `--x` | string | - | --chart-type: the category/itemName encode variable (a query match/outcome var) |
| `--y` | string | - | --chart-type: the value encode variable (a query match/outcome var) |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

## dashboards charts batch

Batch-add charts from a file, paced under quota and idempotent (guarded)

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl dashboards charts batch <dashboard-id> --file <charts.json> [flags]
```

```text
Author a whole dashboard's charts from a JSON array file in one guarded run.
Each spec is {title, query, chartType, x, y, seriesBy, tileType, layout,
interval, datasource, visualization} (same fields as `charts add`). The build
is:
  - validated UP FRONT (every spec's chart-type encode vars vs its query), so a
    bad spec fails before any chart is written;
  - idempotent — a chart whose title already exists on the dashboard is SKIPPED,
    so a re-run after a partial failure converges instead of duplicating;
  - paced (--pace between adds, default 1s) to stay under the per-minute chart
    quota (the transport also retries a 429).
Guarded: dry-run by default, --yes to apply. Re-pull afterwards.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--file` | string | - | JSON array of chart specs (required) |
| `--pace` | duration | 1s | delay between adds to stay under the chart quota |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

## dashboards charts edit

Edit a chart's query, visualization, or layout in place (guarded)

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl dashboards charts edit <dashboard-id> --chart-id <id> [flags]
```

```text
Edit an existing chart via :editChart, in place (no remove + re-add that would
churn the chart id / grid position / order). Change any of:
  --query / --query-file   the YARA-L query (etag-guarded dashboardQuery);
  --visualization <json>   the raw visualization, OR --chart-type bar|line|pie|
    table with --x/--y/--series-by to GENERATE it (encode vars validated against
    the chart's query);
  --layout <json>          the chart's grid position (applied via the
    dashboard's definition.charts — chart_layout is not an :editChart field —
    preserving every other chart).
At least one is required. Guarded: dry-run by default, --yes to apply.
```

| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--filters` | stringSlice | - | set the chart's filter bindings (e.g. GlobalTimeFilter) |
| `--interval` | string | - | optional new query input interval (JSON) |
| `--layout` | string | - | new chart layout on the 96-column grid (JSON) |

## dashboards charts run

Execute a chart's query and print the computed values (read-only)

```text
secopsctl dashboards charts run <dashboard-id> --chart-id <id> [flags]
```

```text
Execute a chart's stored query via `dashboardQueries:execute` and print the
computed rows/series — the values a chart actually renders (legend labels,
axis categories, series values), which `dashboards charts` (config only)
never shows. Read-only. --json for the raw result, --clear-cache to bypass the
```

|---|---|---|---|
| `--chart-id` | string | - | id (or resource name) of the chart to execute (required) |

| `--filter` | string | - | optional dashboard-filter JSON array applied to the query |
| `--table` | bool | false | render the query result as a text table instead of raw JSON |

## dashboards duplicate

Duplicate a dashboard to a new independent dashboard (guarded)

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl dashboards duplicate <dashboard-id> --name <name> --access <type> [flags]
```

```text
Copy a dashboard under a new display name and access type. By default this
uses the server `:duplicate` verb — the same path the web console's Duplicate
action takes — which creates an independent copy: the new dashboard gets its
own freshly-minted charts and queries (not references to the source's), so it
renders and deletes like any other dashboard. This is also the supported way to
set the otherwise-immutable `access` on the copy.

--deep-copy rebuilds the copy client-side instead: fetch every chart and
recreate it FRESH, without the server verb. A fallback for when the server-side
copy is unavailable. Guarded: dry-run by default, --yes to apply. Re-pull
afterwards so local mirrors live.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--access` | string | - | access type for the copy: DASHBOARD_PRIVATE \| DASHBOARD_PUBLIC (required) |
| `--deep-copy` | bool | false | rebuild the copy client-side instead of using the server :duplicate verb (fallback) |
| `--description` | string | - | optional description for the copy (inherits the source's when empty) |
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--name` | string | - | display name for the copy (required) |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

## dashboards filters set

Set the global time range filter on a dashboard (guarded)

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl dashboards filters set <dashboard-id> --time <N> --unit <UNIT> [flags]
```

```text
Set or replace the dashboard's global time range filter. The filter
controls the default time window for all charts. Common values:
  --time 1 --unit HOUR     (last hour)
  --time 24 --unit HOUR    (last 24 hours)
  --time 7 --unit DAY      (last 7 days)
  --time 14 --unit DAY     (last 14 days)
  --time 30 --unit DAY     (last 30 days)

Use --apply-to to bind the filter to charts in the same PATCH:
  --apply-to all           bind GlobalTimeFilter to every chart
  --apply-to id1,id2       bind to specific chart IDs (bare or full ref)
Without --apply-to, only definition.filters is updated (chart bindings unchanged).
Guarded: dry-run by default, --yes to apply.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--apply-to` | string | - | bind the filter to charts: "all" or comma-separated chart IDs |
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--time` | int | 0 | time range value (e.g. 24) |
| `--unit` | string | - | time range unit: HOUR \| DAY \| WEEK \| MONTH |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.


## dashboards lint

Static analysis of a dashboard's charts — check for common issues (read-only)

```text
secopsctl dashboards lint <dashboard-id>
```

```text
Checks every chart for:
  1. "none" legend — a legends array on a single-series chart renders
     "none" as the label in the console (fixable: remove legends).
  2. Long axis labels — email addresses / FQDNs without re.capture()
     truncation, unreadable at >30 chars (fixable: --strip-domain).
  3. Time-range desync — per-chart query input.relativeTime differs
     from the dashboard's global time filter (fixable: --sync-time).
  4. Missing chart title — untitled charts are hard to identify.
  5. Overlapping grid positions — two charts occupying the same cells.
  6. Reserved variable names ($rule, $events, $entity, …) — the chart
     saves but fails at execute time and renders blank (rename the variable).
Read-only — no API writes.
```

| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

## dashboards verify

Execute every chart and flag the ones returning no rows or an error (read-only)

```text
secopsctl dashboards verify [<dashboard-id>] [flags]
```

```text
A dashboard health check: execute each chart's query (`dashboardQueries:execute`)
and report which charts return an ERROR or 0 rows (EMPTY) vs OK — so a blank or
broken chart is caught headless / in CI without opening the UI. Queries using a
reserved variable name ($rule, $events, $entity, …) are flagged as errors
statically — they can execute clean yet render blank in the console. Charts run in
parallel (--concurrency, default 8) so a many-chart dashboard verifies in
seconds. Pass --all to health-check every dashboard in the instance (a fleet
rollup; one row per dashboard). Read-only; exits non-zero (2) when any chart is
empty or errored. --json for the full report.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--all` | bool | false | health-check every dashboard in the instance (fleet rollup, one row per dashboard) |
| `--clear-cache` | bool | false | bypass the query cache (read from the database) |
| `--concurrency` | int | 8 | max charts to execute in parallel (lower it if you hit rate limits) |
| `--include-curated` | bool | false | with --all: also verify CURATED (Google-managed) dashboards, not just your CUSTOM ones |
